page: Google Cloud Platform n4a-highmem-1 is an ARM64-based virtual machine instance featuring a single dedicated vCPU powered by a 3.4 GHz ARMv8 Neoverse-N3 processor. This single-core configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 112 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks reflect the single-core architecture of the instance. The Neoverse-N3 processor delivers average single-core CPU performance in stress-ng testing and strong single-threaded gzip compression speeds of 32.47 GB/sec. However, due to the single-vCPU limitation, multi-core CPU benchmarks and Passmark CPU scores fall into the lower percentiles. Memory performance is characterized by a weak Passmark memory score and uncached large-block read and write bandwidths of 23.47 GB/sec and 24.16 GB/sec, respectively. Database operations and Redis SET operations also perform in the lower tiers, with Redis achieving 2.33 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n4a-highmem-1 offers a dedicated ARM core and a relatively high memory allocation without the overhead of multi-core licensing or unneeded compute resources. This makes it a viable option for lightweight, memory-sensitive workloads that do not require parallel processing. Suitable use cases include single-threaded applications, basic web serving, lightweight database operations, and simple background tasks or utility scripts that benefit from 8 GB of RAM but only require a single dedicated CPU thread.
